adjective after noun in phrases such as mi amiga inglesa
basic plural articles and nouns: el -> los, la -> las, vowel + s

guided_production_notes: Successful final role-play as Ivan with Teresa using greetings, identity, state, journey, and tiredness response.
Keyboard limitation accepted for inverted punctuation and accents; tutor should continue showing correct forms while accepting plain keyboard input.
Short review: produced ¿Cómo estás?, Estoy un poco cansado, and El viaje es bueno after one prompt.
Completed Exercise 1 introductions; main correction was spelling/capitalization, not structure.
Completed Exercise 2 article drill; corrected el problema after initial la problema; previewed Exercise 3 with ¿Estás ocupado?
Short Exercise 3 session: learner produced ¿Estás ocupado?, ¿Estás enfermo?, ¿Estás libre?; corrected spelling of cansado and repaired Tu hermano es... to Tu hermano está...

30-minute session: learner finished sister prompts in Exercise 3, completed plural Exercise 4, and completed Exercise 5 controlled production. Keep estoy, está, cansado/cansada, and libre active for review.
Post-session learner request: explicitly highlight estoy vs está vs estás, repeat enfermo/enferma, and repeat pero next session.

Three-minute review: learner correctly produced ¿Estás enfermo?, Mi hermano no está ocupado, Estoy enfermo, pero mi hermano está libre, and ¿Tu hermana está ocupada?; repaired cansado/cansada after explicit memory drill. Keep cansado/cansada active because learner reported the word is hard to remember.

Short lesson: learner completed Exercise 6 and Exercise 7. Main repairs were cansado/cansada spelling, Juan's brother as el hermano de Juan, su hermana instead of tu hermana for his/her sister, and using ¿Cómo está...? for the Exercise 6 pattern.
End review: learner selected estoy/estás/está correctly, produced Mi hermana está cansada and Estoy libre, but used a non-Spanish form for my brother is ill; reinforce Mi hermano está enfermo.

Short session: learner rewrote Dialogue 1 for Max and Claudio at night. Main repair was Buenas noches and recalling cansado after initially writing casando. Learner completed the final mixed review sentence correctly.

15-minute Dialogue 2 session: learner began the introductions dialogue and practiced Éste/Ésta es, Encantado/a, Muchas gracias, mamá, bienvenida a nuestra casa, amigo/amiga, inglés/inglesa, and el/la hermano/a de. Main repairs were consado/consada -> cansado/cansada, muy bien -> muchas gracias for thanks, amigo inglés word order, and using Éste for masculine introductions.
